Rashi on Nedarim 50a:1:1.english: He lifted the mat - He raised the mat upon which he was sitting.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:1:2.english: And he said to the messenger - who went to his house.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:1:3.hebrew: חזי מאי איכא - ראה כמה עושר יש לי, שנעשה לו נס ונתמלא כל אותו מקום זהובים:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:1:3.english: See what there is - See how much wealth I have, for a miracle was performed for him and that entire place was filled with gold coins.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:2:1.english: And she married him in the winter - In the wintertime.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:3:1.hebrew: הוה גנו בי תיבנא - היו ישנים בין התבן, שלא היו להם כרים וכסתות:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:3:1.english: They would sleep in a storehouse of straw - They would sleep among the straw, for they did not have pillows or cushions.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:3:2.english: [He] was picking straw from his hair - He was gathering the straw from his hair.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:3:3.hebrew: אי הוי לי רמינא לך ירושלים דדהבא - אם יהיה לי סיפוק שאתעשר, אעשה לך ירושלים של זהב, בתי נפש שמצויירת בכל ענייני ירושלים. והיינו דאמרינן במסכת שבת (דף נט.): עיר ירושלים של זהב, כדעבד ליה רבי עקיבא לדביתהו:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:3:3.english: If I had [the means], I would place upon you a Jerusalem of Gold - If I have sufficient means such that I become wealthy, I will make for you a Jerusalem of Gold, a batei nefesh [ornament] that is depicted with all the features of Jerusalem. And this is what we say in Tractate Shabbat (59a): "A City of Jerusalem of Gold, like [that which] Rabbi Akiva made for his wife."

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:3:4.hebrew: אתא אליהו קרא אבבא וכו' - עבד הכי משום קורת רוח להן, דלדידיה לא היה לו אפילו תבן כמו להם:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:3:4.english: Elijah came [and] called at the door, etc. - [He] did this for their peace of mind, [showing] that he did not even have straw like they [did].

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:4:1.english: Your father behaved well toward you - That he vowed [to bar] you from his property.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:4:2.hebrew: חדא דלא דמי לך - שהוא גרוע ממך, ועוד שמניחך באלמנות חיות, שהרי הניחך כמה שנים:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:4:2.english: One [reason is] that he is not similar to you - For he is inferior to you, and furthermore, that he leaves you in living widowhood, for he has left you [for] several years.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:5:1.hebrew: יודע צדיק נפש בהמתו - אית דאמרי דאיהי הות ידעה דר' עקיבא הוה, ואמרה ליה דלא מיתגניא בעיניה. ואית דאמרי דלא הות ידעה, אלא הכי קא אמרה: דצדיק לא מבזה לאינשי:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:5:1.english: A righteous man regards the life of his beast - There are those who say that she knew that it was Rabbi Akiva, and she was saying to him that she is not unseemly in his eyes. And there are those who say that she did not know [that it was he], rather, this is what she was saying: that a righteous man does not demean people.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:5:2.english: Mine and yours is hers - All that I have learned is through her.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:6:1.hebrew: מן שית מילי איעתר רבי עקיבא מן כלבא שבוע - דפליג ליה בנכסיה:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:6:1.english: From six things Rabbi Akiva became wealthy: from Kalba Savua - For he [Kalba Savua] shared his property with him.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:6:2.hebrew: ומן אילא דספינתא דכל ספינתא עבדין ליה מן עינא - עושין להן מן אותו ענין של איל. ואית דגרסי "מין עיינא" — היו עושין כמין צאן של עץ, והיו נותנים בו כספם:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:6:2.english: And from the ram of a ship, as for every ship they make for it min ayna - They make for them from that same matter of a ram. And some read min ayna [meaning a species of sheep]: they would make a kind of wooden sheep and would place their money in it.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:6:3.english: They forgot it on the seashore - That they forgot that ram on the seashore, and Rabbi Akiva found it.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:7:2.hebrew: ארבעה זוזי לספונאי - ליורדי הים, לריוח:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:7:2.english: Four zuz to sailors - To seafarers, for profit.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:7:3.english: Bring me something - Bring me anything.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:7:4.english: Our master upon it - May our master wait upon it until we bring you more.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:7:5.english: For on one occasion a ship sank - And all the money that was in the ship was placed in that log.

Rashi on Nedarim 50a:8:1.hebrew: ומן מטרוניתא - שפעם אחת הוצרכו חכמים ממון הרבה לבית המדרש, ושיגרו את ר' עקיבא אצל מטרוניתא אחת, ולוה ממנה ממון גדול. וכשנתנה לו, אמרה לו: מי יהיה לי ערב שתפרע לי לזמן קבוע? אמר לה: מי שתרצה. אמרה לו: הקב"ה והים — שהיה ביתה על שפת הים. אמר לה ר"ע: כן יהיה. כשהגיע הזמן, חלה ר"ע ולא היה יכול להביא הממון. יצאת אותה מטרוניתא על שפת הים ואמרה: רבש"ע, גלוי וידוע לפניך כי לך ולים הזה האמנתי מעותי! הכניס הקב"ה רוח שטות בלבו של קיסר, ונכנס' לבית גנזיו ונטלה קרטלית וזרקה לים, והשליכה הים לפתח ביתה של אותה מטרוניתא, ונטלתה. ולאחר זמן הביא לה ר' עקיבא הממון, ואמר לה: אל יחר ליך שלא הבאתי לך הממון בזמן שקבענו, שחליתי. אמרה לו: יהא הכל שלך, שממוני בא לידי בזמנו! וספרה לו כל המעשה, ונתנה לו מתנות גדולות, ופטרתו לשלום:
Rashi on Nedarim 50a:8:1.english: And from a lady - For once the Sages needed much money for the house of study, and they sent Rabbi Akiva to a certain noblewoman, and he borrowed a large sum of money from her. When she gave [it] to him, she said to him: "Who will be a guarantor for me that you will repay me at the fixed time?" He said to her: "Whomever you wish." She said to him: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, and the sea" — for her house was on the seashore. Rabbi Akiva said to her: "So it shall be." When the time arrived, Rabbi Akiva fell ill and could not bring the money. That noblewoman went out to the seashore and said: "Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that to You and to this sea I entrusted my money!" The Holy One, Blessed be He, put a spirit of folly into Caesar's heart, and [she] entered his treasury, took a chest, and threw it into the sea; and the sea cast it up at the door of that noblewoman's house, and she took it. After some time, Rabbi Akiva brought her the money and said to her: "Do not be angry with me that I did not bring you the money at the time we fixed, for I fell ill." She said to him: "Let it all be yours, for my money came into my hands on time!" And she told him the entire incident, gave him great gifts, and sent him off in peace.

Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:1:1.hebrew: דלי ציפתא - פירוש: הגביה המחצלת, וסמך שימצא שם מעות הרבה בנס:
Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:1:1.english: He lifted the mat [tzifeta] - Explanation: He lifted the mat, and trusted that he would find much money there through a miracle.

Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:3:1.english: They would sleep in straw - On account of poverty.

Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:3:2.english: "Gathering straw for him" - From that which had caught in his hair.

Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:3:3.hebrew: רמינא ליך ירושלים דדהבא - וכן עשה, כדאיתא בשבת (דף נט.):
Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:3:3.english: "I would place on you a Jerusalem of Gold" - And so he did, as it is found in Shabbat (59a).

Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:4:1.english: That he is not similar to you - [Meaning,] he is not worthy or fitting for you.

Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:6:1.english: The ram of a ship [eila disfineta] - For all ships, they make a ram of gold.

Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:8:1.hebrew: ומן מטרונית' - פעם אחת הוצרכו תלמידי רבי עקיבא למעות, הלכו אצל מטרוניתא ללוות ממנה. אמרה להם: איני מאמנת. אמר לה רבי עקיבא: מי את חפצה שאתן ליך ערב? אמרה לו: מי שאמר והיה העולם, וים הגדול. וכשהגיע הזמן חלה רבי עקיבא ולא בא. הלכה על שפת הים, אמרה: רבש"ע, היום חלה רבי עקיבא עבדך, והוא העמידך ערב לי. מה עשה הקב"ה? באותו היום נשטית בת קיסר ונטלה קופסא מליאה כסף וזהב והטילה לים, וצפה ובאת לאותו מקום, ונטלה אותו ומצאה בה ממון גדול. וכשנתרפא רבי עקיבא בא אצלה, ואמר: גלוי וידוע לפני מי שאמר והיה העולם שחליתי באותו הזמן, עכשיו הרי כל ממונך בידי. וסיפרה לו כל המעשה, והכניסתו בבית גנזיה, ונתנה לו מתנות גדולות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 50a:8:1.english: And from a lady - Once, the students of Rabbi Akiva needed money, [so] they went to a lady to borrow from her. She said to them: I do not trust [you]. Rabbi Akiva said to her: Whom do you wish that I give you as a guarantor? She said to him: He who spoke and the world came into being, and the Great Sea. When the time [for repayment] arrived, Rabbi Akiva fell ill and did not come. She went to the seashore [and] said: Master of the Universe, today Rabbi Akiva Your servant fell ill, and he appointed You as a guarantor for me. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? On that very day, the Caesar's daughter went insane, took a chest full of silver and gold, and cast it into the sea; and it floated and came to that place, and she took it and found a great fortune inside it. When Rabbi Akiva recovered, he came to her and said: It is revealed and known before He who spoke and the world came into being that I was ill at that time; now, behold, all of your money is in my hand [to repay you]. And she told him the entire story, brought him into her treasure house, and gave him great gifts.
